reader.requirement: At --std 85 literal-1 of an indexed file's ASSIGN clause must be a nonnumeric literal and not a figurative constant (any figurative, including ALL literal); implementor-name-1 and the literal's value are implementor-defined (here: the host file name, optionally led by a DISK/PRINTER device class).

edition-consulted.switches: sortMerge1985 = kind == SortMerge && DialectLevel < 2002 suppresses the deferred EntryShapeFindings (numeric literal, figurative constant, list shape) for a 1985 SORT-MERGE file only

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: for an indexed file the deferred findings are reported at every edition; only a 1985 sort-merge (SD) file takes the other arm, which this rule does not reach.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb1078 covers zero-length and SPACE on sequential files; pb829 the device-class list. Numeric, other figuratives and ALL literal on an INDEXED file at 85 probed here.

probes.printed: error COBOL2645: ASSIGN TO 12345: literal-1 shall be an alphanumeric literal
error COBOL2645: ASSIGN TO -5: literal-1 shall be an alphanumeric literal
error COBOL2645: ASSIGN TO SPACE: literal-1 shall not be a figurative constant
error COBOL2645: ASSIGN TO ALL"AB": literal-1 shall not be a figurative constant
probes.expected: refused: ALL literal is a figurative constant
nonnumeric literal accepted, file written and read
implementor list DISK literal accepted per DOC-A.1-71

citations.check: OK  §1985:IX.2.3.3 SR3  (2.3.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR3

reader.notes: The grammar admits any literal and AssignTargetRule screens it by name; the numeric and figurative arms are deferred to FileControlKeyRules.Screen so that only the 1985 sort-merge entry (which has no such rule) escapes them. Indexed files at 85 take the same reporting arm as 2023. Messages cite §2023:12.4.5.2 SR4.

refuter.evidence: Class c (later forms 85 must refuse): r2nat ASSIGN TO N"r2nat.dat" -> COBOL2645 'shall be an alphanumeric literal' + COBOL0900 national literal requires COBOL-2002; r2hex X"..." -> COBOL0900 hex literal requires 2002; r2cat "r2" & "cat.dat" -> COBOL0900 concatenation requires 2002; r2using ASSIGN TO DISK USING WS-NAME -> COBOL0900 USING phrase requires 2002. Class d: r2lowv LOW-VALUES, r2allz ALL ZERO, r2spaces SPACES -> COBOL2645 'shall not be a figurative constant'. r2dataname ASSIGN TO WS-NAME (a WORKING-STORAGE name) compiles and runs at 85, but the generated code registers it as the implementor-name "WS-NAME" (RegisterIndexed("R2::IX", "WS-NAME", ...); the file created is ws-name.txt, not the item's value r2-ws.dat), the 1985 implementor-name-1 reading SR3 leaves to the implementor. cite.py: OK  §1985:IX.2.3.3 SR3  (2.3.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR3.
